comparison: Both evaluations support the CRISPR screen findings (C6, C7, C43, C45) identifying COMMD3 as a regulator. OpenEval additionally discusses C44 and C47 (Commander-independent function conclusion), with C47 also appearing in peer R13. Both find the genetic screen evidence compelling.

Perfect agreement on essentiality screen data (C8, C46). Both evaluations accept this negative result without concerns, though peer review treats it as contextual rather than central to main findings.

Both support the GLUT-SPR surface reduction findings (C9, C10, C48, C49) using flow cytometry and imaging. OpenEval additionally discusses C51. Both accept the cross-cell-type validation and quantitative data.

Perfect agreement on endosomal phenotypes (C11, C12, C13, C14, C35). Both evaluations accept the imaging data showing enlarged endosomes, GLUT-SPR accumulation, and Rab5 colocalization as evidence for recycling defects.

Perfect agreement on comparative KO experiments (C15, C16, C17, C18, C19, C50) demonstrating Commander-independent COMMD3 function. Both treat this as a central, well-supported conclusion distinguishing COMMD3-specific from Commander-dependent effects.

Both support COMMD3 upregulation in Commander-deficient cells (C20, C52, C53, C54). OpenEval emphasizes C55 (COMMD3 exists outside Commander), while peer review accepts the interdependent stability observations. Both see this as evidence for dual functionality.

Partial overlap on C20 and C55. Peer R5 additionally covers gain/loss-of-function experiments (C21, C57-C61) that OpenEval addresses in R7. Both support COMMD3's independent function through complementary evidence.

Strong overlap on gain/loss-of-function experiments (C21, C57, C58, C59, C60, C61). Both evaluations accept the genetic evidence, with OpenEval particularly emphasizing the double KO experiment (C59) as ruling out indirect effects.
Both support domain mapping (C22, C66) showing NTD mediates Commander-independent function. OpenEval additionally discusses C3, C62-C65. Both accept the rescue experiments with appropriate controls.

Both support COMMD3-ARF1 interaction (C23, C24). OpenEval additionally covers C67. Peer review also addresses C4 and C25 (covered in OpenEval R10). Both accept proteomics discovery and co-IP validation.

Partial overlap on ARF1 interaction evidence (C4, C25). OpenEval R10 focuses on stabilization mechanism (C26, C27, C36, C70), while peer R7 covers broader interaction data. Both support the COMMD3-ARF1 relationship.
Both support ARF1 stabilization by COMMD3 (C26, C27, C70). OpenEval additionally discusses C4, C25, C36. Both accept the stabilization experiments as supporting the mechanistic model.

Both address the integrative conclusion (C36) that COMMD3 stabilizes ARF1 for cargo recycling. Peer R12 treats this as the main supported conclusion, while OpenEval R10 focuses on the experimental evidence for stabilization.
Perfect agreement on ARF1 overexpression rescue (C28). Both evaluations accept this as strong functional evidence that ARF1 acts downstream of COMMD3 in the pathway.

Both support AlphaFold3 structural predictions (C29, C30, C31, C32). OpenEval additionally discusses C69. Both accept high confidence scores and selective GTP-ARF1 recognition as providing mechanistic insight.

Both address mutagenesis validation (C5, C33, C34, C91), but with different evaluations. OpenEval finds it well-supported, while peer review rates it UNCERTAIN due to missing validation that the mutant disrupts COMMD3-ARF1 interaction and lacks ITGA6 rescue testing.

Both address Commander-independent COMMD3 function (C47 in OpenEval R1, C2/C3/C47 in peer R13). OpenEval supports this from CRISPR screen data, while peer review accepts it as the study's main finding with solid evidence.
Both address C3 (NTD mediates Commander-independent function). OpenEval R8 supports this through domain mapping, while peer R13 accepts it as part of the novel Commander-independent role conclusion.

Both support background knowledge about Commander and Retromer complexes (C1, C37-C42, C90). OpenEval and peer review both accept this as accurately presented foundational context with appropriate citations.

Strong agreement on speculative claims (C56, C71, C72, C75-C78, C85-C87, C89). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN noting lack of direct experimental support, while peer review accepts them as appropriately distinguished speculation rather than definitive conclusions.
Partial overlap on literature context (C92-C97 in OpenEval, C73-C74, C79-C84, C88 in peer review). Both evaluations accept this contextual information as accurately summarizing established knowledge.
Strong overlap on contextual literature claims (C73, C74, C79-C84, C88). OpenEval additionally covers C92-C97. Both accept this as appropriate framing of the study's significance and knowledge gap.
Both address background claims (C62-C65 in OpenEval R8, broader set in peer R16). Both evaluations accept this contextual information without challenge as foundational knowledge.
Minimal overlap on C67 (ARF1 proteomic identification). OpenEval supports the discovery method, while peer R16 treats it as accepted background/methodological context.
Minimal overlap on C69 (structural modeling context). OpenEval supports the AlphaFold predictions, while peer R16 implicitly accepts structural approaches as part of accepted methodology.
